intro.h1: Stationhead is the home of social listening.
intro.lead: Artists and fans listening to the same song at the same time. Every play runs through the listener's own paid account, so every play is a real stream.
body: {{CountCap}} {{thing}} from {{spanPhrase}}. All of them can be played back.

events.herolbl: listeners on release day, the biggest show in two months
body: Three shows opened for the release. The chat ran in Thai, Indonesian and English.

events.herolbl: streams from 7,546 people, on eight songs
body: Eight songs, played over and over, from the group's own account.
The official account ran the listening party for NORMAL.
Release day, announced by the group. Thirteen songs in under an hour.

events.herolbl: listeners bought the record during the show
body: Online retail converts in low single digits. This converted at ten percent.
A fan ran the show, not the label.

events.herolbl: messages a minute, three years after release
body: A Tuesday night, for a three year old album.

events.herolbl: for a tenth anniversary, hosted by the group
body: Ten years of catalogue, played end to end from the official account.
An album turning one year old. Nothing released, nothing announced.

events.herolbl: came for a label talk, with no band members on
body: Billed as label staff and a guest. Five thousand people stayed two hours.

events.herolbl: on the mic, on a fan's show
body: She walked in, spoke, then stayed in the chat.

events.herolbl: streams in six days, with nothing promoted
body: No release, no campaign, no spend. Fans opened all five.

events.herolbl: plays in a day, with the group hosting
body: The group hosted four nights running and took the mic every night.

pattern.h2: Most of this was not scheduled by anyone.
body: A three year old album. A tenth anniversary. A label talk with no band on it. Eight songs played twelve times each.
Fans open most of these shows. When the artist turns up, they walk into one that is already full.
pattern.note: Streams are plays of at least thirty seconds, counted during the show, queried on {{figureDates}}. Platform totals are as of 10 September 2026. Chat lines are real messages from the show, shown in the order fans sent them most. Shows older than thirty days have no chat left to quote.

archive.intro: Older shows. The numbers are as they were reported at the time.
archive.emptyNote: Nothing has rolled off the last three weeks yet.

static.h2: It takes a date and an artist handle.
ol: Confirm the channel. If fans built one already, we connect it rather than starting again.
Pick a time that suits the fans, not the office, and tell the regular hosts first. They fill the show before you post anything.
Announce it from the artist account. Date, time, time zone, one link.
Go live from a phone. Connect the streaming account, queue a few songs, say hello.
On air, read names out, take requests, and say the channel stays open when you go.
static.note: One week is comfortable. Two days is possible.

static.h2: Four things, all of them quick.
ul: Digital purchase. The single or album, bought during the show. About a week.
Shopify shop. Your existing store, opened inside the show. About a week.
Voice note. Thirty seconds recorded on a phone, for when a live date will not work. Two days.
Fan Channel. The permanent home fans join once and keep between releases. A few days.
static.note: To start we need the artist handle, a date, and anything you want to sell.
